17:31 Local Time, 21:31 GMT, 03:01 IST: What a response from Pakistan! They haven't just fought their way back into the contest - they've bulldozed their way back and now hold the upper hand. Trailing by just 78 runs with 8 wickets still in hand, the visitors are in complete control. When West Indies were bowled out for 344 in the morning session, it looked like they had posted an above-par total on a surface offering assistance to the spinners. But a combination of positive batting and ordinary bowling has allowed Pakistan to seize the initiative. Unlike their counterparts, the West Indies spinners couldn't extract the same amount of turn, while there was very little on offer for the seamers.

371 runs today are the most scored in a day's play in a Test on West Indies soil since 2008.

Even so, the bowling lacked consistency as Azan Awais got off to a flying start and brought up a confident half-century. That laid the perfect platform for Shafique and Babar. The pair scored freely, rarely looked troubled and stitched together an unbeaten 168-run stand for the third wicket. Shafique, who came in for the injured Masood after the latter's century in the first Test, capped off a magnificent, chanceless innings with a well-deserved hundred late in the day. At the other end, Babar has been elegance personified, playing with his customary assurance. The two, along with the remaining batters, will now look to bat West Indies out of the contest. Can the hosts produce a fightback on Day 3, or will Pakistan continue their march? Join us tomorrow to find out. Goodbye..

Asad Shafiq | Pakistan batting coach: [On Pakistan's position at stumps after reaching 266/2] Yeah, it's quite satisfying day for me as a batting coach. I mean, the way Abdullah and Babar played and that partnership they gave, it's quite remarkable. And I think that's the thing we were missing from the last 2-3 Test matches. And they took the responsibility. And it's very satisfying for me as a batting coach. [On what impressed him most about Abdullah Shafique's century and the partnership] I think Abdullah Shafiq, he joined the team very recently, but he scored heavily in the domestic tournaments. And he saw this opportunity, and he grabs that with both hands. And I think the hallmark of his innings was he was putting away the bad deliveries really well and respected the good deliveries. [On Pakistan's approach for Day 3] I think the position we are in right now, if we really, if we will bat well tomorrow as well, we will be in that dominating position. From there, we can dictate this game.
